reviews.one_line_contribution: Two auditing instruments for experience-memory claims on template-generated agent benchmarks: a leave-neighbourhood-out curve that plots the paired memory-minus-memoryless delta against the structural distance from the test task to its nearest stored solved episode (store size held constant by matched random removal), and a stream-order-randomization estimator that turns 'a near-duplicate solved predecessor exists' into a within-task randomized treatment, with a non-LLM nearest-neighbour replay control bounding how much of each system's gain is lookup.
reviews.closest_prior_work: arXiv:2608.18066, 'On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification' (2026-08-18, verified via s2cli/S2, 1 citation) is the sharpest threat and the proposal does not cite it: it is a re-evaluation of two memory-based self-improving agent methods explicitly broadened along variance and task-order axes, i.e. it already occupies the proposal's second instrument and its rhetorical hook ('task-order variance is not noise'). Its stated explanation is task and environment underspecification, not near-duplicate predecessor leakage, so it is a partial rather than a full collision — but it means the order-permutation observation is no longer new, only newly parameterized, and a reviewer will ask what the LNO stratification adds beyond what 2608.18066 already reports. Second threat: arXiv:2608.00155 (AgentStream, 2026-07-31, verified via s2cli/HF), which evaluates self-evolving agents under streaming tasks and concludes that reliability depends on model capability and stream composition — 'stream composition' is close to the proposal's predecessor-density variable, again uncited. Third: arXiv:2605.24117 (SkillEvolBench, verified, 2026-05-22), cited by the proposal, which organizes tasks into families with shared latent procedures and finds agents adapt locally but rarely form robust reusable skills — the mechanism the leakage account predicts, one distance-stratification away from the headline. On the QA side, arXiv:2606.14571 (StreamMemBench, 2026-06-12, from the novelty card) already makes the 'tasks are solvable without retrieving the intended evidence' argument, and arXiv:2606.29914 (MemDelta, verified 2026-06-29) already established the controlled-baseline/hidden-confound genre for memory evaluation. None of these does the leave-neighbourhood-out curve on ALFWorld/WebShop with matched-size removal, which is the residual novelty; it is real but narrow, and the underlying suspicion (ExpeL's 'unseen' ALFWorld split shares all six templates with the training pool) is a widely voiced folk criticism rather than a discovery.
reviews.strongest_objection: The paper is a category argument disguised as a measurement: retrieving a solved near-duplicate IS what episodic experience memory is for, so 'the gain concentrates at d<=1' describes the mechanism working, not leakage, unless the proposal argues that the deployment distribution contains far fewer d<=1 tasks than the benchmark does — which it never does. Without a target-distribution argument, P1 holding is fully compatible with every audited system being exactly as useful as advertised, and the headline claim is unearned. Second, and independently damaging: the order-randomization estimator is not the clean within-task randomization it claims. Under prequential evaluation with a growing store, whether a near-duplicate predecessor exists is mechanically correlated with stream position and store size inside every shuffled order, so the model as written (success ~ memory x predecessor-stratum with task/order/seed random effects, no position or store-size term) confounds 'has a near-duplicate predecessor' with 'is late in the stream'. The de-duplicated order compounds this: a greedy no-d<=1-predecessor order is a selected, not a sampled, permutation and necessarily alters the task-type composition of early versus late positions, so P4's flattened slope is expected even under a pure position effect. Third, the compute plan is off by close to an order of magnitude: the LNO grid alone (3 store types x k in {1,3,7} x d in {0..4} x matched-removal control x ~1,300 paired tasks x 2 seeds, plus the memoryless arm) exceeds 100k episodes, not the stated 25k, and the streaming arm at 400 tasks x R=10-20 orders x 2 seeds x memory/memoryless x 3 stores is 50-70k, not 15-25k. Fourth, the ratio-valued predictions (P2's >=50% of the gain, P3's >=70%) are undefined when the denominator is small: this program's own measured memory gain is +0.6pt at 27B against a 0.05-0.14 re-scoring noise floor and a pre-registered MDE near 2.5pt, so on the 27B backbone the aggregate gain may not clear zero and every percentage-of-gain prediction becomes uninterpretable with unbounded CIs. No minimum-aggregate-gain precondition is pre-registered.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Pre-register a gate: P2 and P3 fire only when the aggregate memory gain on that backbone/environment clears a stated threshold (e.g. the 2.5-point MDE) with a CI excluding zero; otherwise report absolute per-stratum deltas and state in advance that a null aggregate gain makes the leakage decomposition vacuous rather than confirmed. (2) Add stream position and store size as fixed effects in the streaming model and report the predecessor coefficient adjusted for both; better, use a position-matched contrast — pair each (task, order) where the task sits at position p with a d<=1 predecessor against the same task at position p in an order without one, holding position exactly rather than modelling it away. Replace the greedy de-duplicated order with a type-composition-matched constrained sampler and report a null slope band over constrained orders that do permit near-duplicates. (3) Make the normative claim testable: state what fraction of d<=1 tasks a realistic deployment stream contains, or reframe as 'here is the LNO curve and how to report it' and drop 'leakage' from the headline — the reporting-standard framing survives every outcome, the leakage framing needs an argument the proposal does not have. (4) Cite and differentiate arXiv:2608.18066 and arXiv:2608.00155; the order-variance observation must be positioned as prior work, with near-duplicate leakage as the competing explanation to 2608.18066's underspecification account, and ideally tested head-to-head (underspecification predicts order variance that survives conditioning on predecessor distance; leakage predicts it largely vanishes) — that contrast would be a substantially stronger paper than the current one. (5) Cut the grid to fit the node: fix k=3 for the LNO sweep, use one store type for the streaming arm, and report the honest episode count.
reviews.missing_baseline: A static fixed-exemplar control: a non-retrieved, distance-uncontrolled in-context demonstration set (the conventional two-exemplar ReAct ALFWorld prompt) held constant across every condition, plus a random-retrieval arm in which the store is intact but the k injected items are drawn uniformly instead of by nearest neighbour. The proposal never states whether its 'memoryless agent' carries the standard fixed exemplars; if it is zero-shot while every memory arm receives k exemplars, the entire measured gain is exemplar presence and the d-stratification only measures how much better a near exemplar is than a far one — a different and much weaker claim. The random-retrieval arm is what separates 'the retriever finds near-duplicates' from 'the store holds nothing useful beyond d=2', a distinction the LNO removal design confounds (removing a neighbourhood removes both the near-duplicate and the store's highest-quality content; matched random removal equalizes size but not quality). The relevance-matched d=2 decoy is a partial substitute, but it is a single substitution at one distance rather than a k-matched arm across the sweep.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision on the full central claim, but the proposal's own check is materially incomplete in exactly the window the field moves fastest in, and it admits this: it reports six further WebSearch queries refused for an exhausted budget, and its newest cited ID is from 2026-06. All of my queries were answered by channel (a), the s2cli command (S2+HF); WebSearch was unavailable in this session and WebFetch is blocked, so channel (b) answered nothing. Q1 'near-duplicate leakage in agent experience memory store-test overlap ALFWorld' (no recency filter): nothing on the mechanism (2607.13157, 2607.05844, 2606.24775, 2605.29463, 2512.16962, 2605.12493 and off-topic systems work). Q2 'task order randomization streaming evaluation memory agent order sensitivity permutation' (--recent): returned arXiv:2608.18066 (2026-08-18, cit 1) and arXiv:2608.00155 (AgentStream, 2026-07-31), both post-dating the proposal's check and both uncited; 2608.18066 re-evaluates two memory-based self-improving methods along variance and task-order axes, pre-empting the order-permutation instrument while attributing fragility to task/environment underspecification rather than near-duplicate predecessors. Only its one-line summary was retrievable (the s2cli 'paper' call returns the same summary and an exact-title query yielded no fuller abstract), so I cannot verify whether it also stratifies by store-test distance; on the evidence I have it is a partial, not a verified, collision. Q3 'ExpeL experience learning insights ALFWorld train test task template overlap generalization': nothing relevant (Synapse 2306.07863 and assorted RL/self-evolution work). Q4 'retrieved in-context example similarity to test instance explains performance gain memorization not generalization' (--recent): 4 hits, none on agent memory. Q5 'self-evolving agent memory gains variance across task orders seeds reproducibility re-evaluation ALFWorld' (--recent): EvoMemBench 2605.18421, MemPro 2606.00619, AdaMEM 2606.05684, MemEvolve 2512.18746 — none randomizes order or stratifies by store-test distance. Q6 'leave-one-out neighborhood split train test similarity stratified evaluation contamination retrieval memory benchmark agent' (--recent): 5 hits, nothing on the mechanism. Q7 'nearest neighbor trajectory replay baseline beats memory framework agent experience reuse lookup' (--recent): CER 2506.06698 and MemCon 2607.13591, no replay-bound control. Q8 'memory gains concentrate on tasks similar to stored solved episodes audit generalization agent' (--recent): 6 hits — 2607.08393 (knowing-using gap in finetuning), 2607.01224 (AutoMem), 2608.00017 (Memory Reward Inflation in self-improving agents, an adjacent self-grading confound), 2606.24595 (MEMPROBE), 2606.05646, 2601.11653 — none stratifies memory gains by store-test distance. ID verification: VERIFIED via s2cli — 2511.20857 (Evo-Memory/ReMem, 2025-11-25), 2512.10696 (ReMe, 2025-12-11), 2504.07952 (Dynamic Cheatsheet), 2605.24117 (SkillEvolBench), 2604.27003, 2606.29914 (MemDelta), 2601.19334, 2603.21636, 2311.01964, plus the two new threats 2608.18066 and 2608.00155. NOT VERIFIED: arXiv:2606.28374 ('Recursive Self-Evolving Agents via Held-Out Selection') — not found on S2 or HF, and the proposal leans on it for the held-out-selection contrast; arXiv:2606.14571 (StreamMemBench) — my verification call timed out, and the proposal itself cites StreamMemBench only as 'ICLR 2026' with a virtual-site URL and no arXiv id, so the reader cannot check it. Judgement of the check itself: the queries are real, specific and honestly reported, which is above average, but a novelty argument silent on the two most recent months that misses a directly on-axis August preprint about task-order variance in memory-based self-improving agents has not established novelty on the order-randomization half.
